title: Derived-section presentation by bounded-below hypersheaves
statement:
A small Grothendieck site is a small category with specified covering sieves, containing the maximal sieve and closed under pullback of sieves and transitivity; a sieve is a collection of arrows with fixed target closed under precomposition. A family covers when its generated sieve covers. No fibre products in the underlying category are required. All sizes use [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $\mathbf D(\Lambda)$ be the enhanced localization of cochain complexes of $\Lambda$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms, retaining derived mapping complexes and all higher composition data [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A $\mathbf D(\Lambda)$-valued hypersheaf is a coherent presheaf $F$ such that for every hypercover $T_\bullet\to T$ the map $F(T)\to\operatorname{holim}_{[n]\in\Delta}F(T_n)$ is an equivalence. Here a hypercover is an augmented simplicial family of representable presheaves whose maps to all matching presheaves are locally surjective after sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]; $F$ on a family is the product of its values. Write $\operatorname{Hyp}_{\ge a}(\mathcal C,\Lambda)$ for the full enhanced category of such $F$ with $H^i(F(T))=0$ for every $T$ and $i<a$, for a fixed integer $a$. Morphisms are coherent natural transformations, and mapping complexes are the derived ends in the coherent presheaf category.

For any such site $\mathcal C$, let $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C,\Lambda)$ be the category of sheaves of modules over the constant sheaf of rings $\Lambda$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Write $\mathbf D_{\ge a}(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C,\Lambda))$ for the full enhanced localization of their complexes whose cohomology sheaves vanish in degrees below $a$. Here $R\Gamma(T,-)$ denotes the right derived functor of evaluation $N\mapsto N(T)$ from module sheaves to $\Lambda$-modules. Derived evaluation defines an equivalence, including derived mapping complexes,
$$M\longmapsto (T\longmapsto R\Gamma(T,M)),\qquad
\mathbf D_{\ge a}(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C,\Lambda))\simeq\operatorname{Hyp}_{\ge a}(\mathcal C,\Lambda).$$
For the inverse image $M$ of $F$, the cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^i(M)$ is the sheafification of $T\mapsto H^i(F(T))$. These equivalences are compatible with changing $a$ and with localization to a slice site: on $\mathcal C/T$, the presheaf for the restricted object has value $R\Gamma(S,M)$ at $(S\to T)$. In particular the compatibility is specified as enhanced natural equivalences, not only isomorphisms of degree-zero morphism groups.

source.place: Tag 0DA2, lemma-hypercovering-equivalence-bounded-modules, is the ordinary total-hypercover descent prototype only. The enhanced derived-section presentation on arbitrary Grothendieck sites is an agent-formulated foundation. Hemo--Richarz--Scholbach, Constructible sheaves on schemes, section 3, printed p.6, discusses the analogous hypercomplete-module model on the pro-etale site and cites SAG Theorem 2.1.2.2. WANTED: an archived enhanced bounded-below derived-section/hypersheaf comparison for arbitrary sites.
